dialogue.content: (こんばんは。本日は宜しくお願いいたします。時間になりましたら始めさせて頂きます。）
dialogue.English: (Good evening. Thank you for coming today. We'll begin when it's time.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそ宜しくお願いします）
dialogue.English: (Thank you. I look forward to our session as well.)

dialogue.content: こんばんは。相談員です。相談にお越し頂きありがとうございます。始めに、年齢・性別・相談内容を教えて下さい。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation. To begin, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 16歳女部活に行きたくない
dialogue.English: I'm a 16-year-old girl, and I don't want to go to my club activity.

dialogue.content: 教えて頂きありがとうございます。どのような事で部活に行きたくないと感じているのですか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. What is it that makes you feel like you don't want to go to your club?

dialogue.content: 先生が嫌いです
dialogue.English: I don't like the teacher.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。先生が嫌だと行きたくなくなりますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It makes sense that you wouldn't want to go if you dislike the teacher.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 先生のどのような事が気になりますか？
dialogue.English: What is it about the teacher that bothers you?

dialogue.content: 怖い、話が長い、お世話が嫌、理不尽
dialogue.English: He's scary, he talks for a long time, I hate doing his personal chores, and he's unreasonable.

dialogue.content: いっぱいあります
dialogue.English: There are a lot of things.

dialogue.content: 色々あるのですね。
dialogue.English: So there are quite a few things.

dialogue.content: はい嫌いです
dialogue.English: Yes, I dislike him.

dialogue.content: ちなみに何部ですか？
dialogue.English: By the way, what club are you in?

dialogue.content: バレーボール部
dialogue.English: The volleyball club.

dialogue.content: マネージャーです
dialogue.English: I'm a manager.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。マネージャーはどれくらいしてるのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. How long have you been a manager?

dialogue.content: 一年です
dialogue.English: For one year.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。今は高校2年生ですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Are you in your second year of high school now?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 部活に行きたくないと思うようになったのは、いつくらいからなのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: About when did you start to feel like you didn't want to go to the club?

dialogue.content: 一年の夏くらいからかな
dialogue.English: I think it was around the summer of my first year.

dialogue.content: そうだっだんですね。かなり長い間、苦しい思いをしながら頑張って続けてきたのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So you've been pushing through and enduring these difficult feelings for quite a long time.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 良く頑張ってこられましたね。。１年の夏に何かきっかけとかあったのですか？
dialogue.English: You've done so well to keep going. Was there something that happened in the summer of your first year that triggered this?

dialogue.content: 3年が引退して１年が怒られるようになったり、仕事が増えて、うまくできなかったり
dialogue.English: The third-years retired, and the first-years started getting yelled at more. The workload increased, and I couldn't do things well.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。初めの事や慣れない事は、上手くいかない事ってありますよね。それで怒られると、嫌な気持ちになるのも無理ないと思いますよ。
dialogue.English: I understand. It's normal for things not to go well when you're doing something for the first time or you're not used to it. It's perfectly understandable that you'd feel upset when you get yelled at for it.

dialogue.content: ちなみにマネージャーは何人いるのですか？
dialogue.English: By the way, how many managers are there?

dialogue.content: はい、怖いです
dialogue.English: Yes, he's scary.

dialogue.content: 三人
dialogue.English: Three.

dialogue.content: 怖いと感じるくらい、厳しい先生なのですね。。マネージャー三人とも同じように怒られてしますのですか？
dialogue.English: So he's such a strict teacher that you feel scared. Do all three managers get yelled at in the same way?

dialogue.content: ごめんなさい。「怒られてしまうのですか？」の誤りです。
dialogue.English: My apologies. That was a typo for "Do you all get yelled at?"

dialogue.content: 私はミスが多いので怒られることが多いです。でも先生は色んな人にいつも怒鳴ってます
dialogue.English: I make a lot of mistakes, so I get scolded a lot. But the teacher is always yelling at all kinds of people.

dialogue.content: そのような状況なのですね。そんな先生について、いつもどのような気持ちになりますか？
dialogue.English: I see that's the situation. How do you usually feel about a teacher like that?

dialogue.content: 怖い、めんどくさい、正しいことはいってるのかもしれないけど
dialogue.English: Scared, annoyed... and maybe what he's saying is right, but...

dialogue.content: 怖い先生だと、あなたが思っている事も言えなかったりするのではないでしょうか。
dialogue.English: When a teacher is scary, it must be hard to say what you're really thinking, isn't it?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 他の２人のマネージャーと、先生の事について話し合ったりしますか？
dialogue.English: Do you ever talk about the teacher with the other two managers?

dialogue.content: みんな嫌いです
dialogue.English: Everyone dislikes him.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。。ちなみに、マネージャーの仕事についてはどうですか？
dialogue.English: I see... By the way, how do you feel about the manager's duties themselves?

dialogue.content: 頼られることは嬉しいです。でも先生の世話は嫌です
dialogue.English: I'm happy when people rely on me. But I hate doing the teacher's personal chores.

dialogue.content: バレー部員の為にお仕事はやりがいがありそうですね。先生のお世話とはどのような事があるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: It sounds like the work you do for the volleyball team members is rewarding. What kind of personal chores for the teacher are there?

dialogue.content: 靴をだす、雨の日は傘をさす、荷物もち、お茶だし
dialogue.English: Taking out his shoes, holding an umbrella on rainy days, carrying his bags, serving tea.

dialogue.content: 誕生日プレゼントをわたす
dialogue.English: Giving him a birthday present.

dialogue.content: そのような事があるのですね。誕生日プレゼントまで渡すのですか。。
dialogue.English: So you have to do things like that. You even give him a birthday present...

dialogue.content: 結婚記念日のプレゼントとか
dialogue.English: Like a wedding anniversary present.

dialogue.content: 個人的は記念日のプレゼントまで。。
dialogue.English: Even presents for his personal anniversaries...

dialogue.content: 先生がしろって言ったんじゃ無くて伝統なんです
dialogue.English: It's not that the teacher told us to do it; it's a tradition.

dialogue.content: でもやめましょうとは言わないです。
dialogue.English: But he doesn't say we should stop.

dialogue.content: 今までずっとマネージャーがされてきたということなのですね。それは、理不尽だと感じるも無理ないですよね。
dialogue.English: So this is something that managers have been doing for a long time. It's no wonder you feel it's unreasonable.

dialogue.content: はいめんどくさいです
dialogue.English: Yes, it's a pain.

dialogue.content: ええ。。そう思われるのも自然な事だと思います。あなたとしては、先生のお世話について、今後どのようにして行きたいと思いますか？
dialogue.English: Yes... I think it's natural to feel that way. As for you, what would you like to do about these chores for the teacher going forward?

dialogue.content: するしかしょうがないです
dialogue.English: I have no choice but to do them.

dialogue.content: そのように感じているのですね。
dialogue.English: That's how you feel about it.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: バレー部の先生は他にいるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Are there any other teachers for the volleyball club?

dialogue.content: いえ、一人です
dialogue.English: No, just him.

dialogue.content: なるほどです。では、その先生がバレー部を見てくれているので、伝統を続けているというわけなのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So, because he's the one in charge of the volleyball club, the tradition continues.

dialogue.content: 先生はバレー部員にも厳しいのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is the teacher also strict with the volleyball players?

dialogue.content: はい私よりも選手は怒られてます
dialogue.English: Yes, the players get yelled at more than I do.

dialogue.content: 強豪校なので
dialogue.English: Because it's a powerhouse school.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。部員の方も先生がいるから試合に勝てる事がある反面、言いたい事が言えないという事があるように思います。
dialogue.English: I see. I imagine that while the teacher may help the team win matches, on the other hand it can make it hard for the members to say what they want to say.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 怒り出したら長いから言いたいことは言えませんめちゃくちゃ怖いし
dialogue.English: Once he starts getting angry, it goes on for a long time, so we can't say what we want. And he's incredibly scary.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。先生という立場ですし、怖いと余計に聞かなくてはという気持ちになりますよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. He's in the position of a teacher, and when he's scary, it makes you feel like you have no choice but to listen.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: あなたは、今後マネージャーを続けていく事については、どのように思っていますか？
dialogue.English: How do you feel about continuing as a manager in the future?

dialogue.content: 辞めたいけど、、
dialogue.English: I want to quit, but...

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。。
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: 言うのが怖いし内申点がもらえなくなります
dialogue.English: I'm scared to say it, and it will affect my school report.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: 今までずっと頑張ってマネージャーをされて来たことは素晴らしい事だと私は感じています。
dialogue.English: I feel that it's wonderful you've worked so hard as a manager for this long.

dialogue.content: ただ、今までお話を聞かせて頂いて
dialogue.English: However, from what you've told me so far,

dialogue.content: 理不尽な事もあり、辞めたい気持ちや、進路が気になる事もあり、部活が負担になっている事も感じています。
dialogue.English: I can also sense that with the unreasonable demands, your desire to quit, and concerns about your future academic path, the club has become a burden.

dialogue.content: はい楽しい時もあるけど、やっぱり先生が高圧的だし、全然遊ぶ暇がないし
dialogue.English: Yes, there are fun times, but the teacher is so overbearing, and I have no time to hang out with friends.

dialogue.content: 遊びたい
dialogue.English: I want to hang out.

dialogue.content: 彼氏も欲しいし
dialogue.English: I want a boyfriend too.

dialogue.content: ええ。ええ。楽しい高校生活を過ごしたいですよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, yes. You want to have an enjoyable high school life, right?

dialogue.content: はい部活と先生の世話で終わっちゃう
dialogue.English: Yes, it all just ends up being club activities and taking care of the teacher.

dialogue.content: あなたの高校生活ですから、あなたが選択して良いのでは思いますがどのように思いますか？
dialogue.English: It's your high school life, so I think you should be the one to choose. What do you think about that?

dialogue.content: 母にも同じことを言われました
dialogue.English: My mother told me the same thing.

dialogue.content: お母さんにも相談されたのですね。
dialogue.English: So you've talked to your mother about it.

dialogue.content: 怒られて泣いて帰った日、辞めたいって
dialogue.English: On a day I came home crying after being yelled at, I told her I wanted to quit.

dialogue.content: そしたらあなたが決めなさいって
dialogue.English: And she said, "You decide."

dialogue.content: ええ。そんな事があったのですね。素敵なお母さんですね。あなたの事を信頼しているからの言葉だと思います。
dialogue.English: I see. So that happened. You have a wonderful mother. I think she said that because she trusts you.

dialogue.content: お母さんは我慢する必要ないって父はそんな経験は社会で役に立つって
dialogue.English: My mom says I don't have to put up with it, but my dad says that kind of experience will be useful in the real world.

dialogue.content: ええ。いろんな選択肢がありますね。勿論、今頑張っている事は役にたつかと思います。もし部活を続けるのであれば、理不尽は部分は校長先生などに相談するという事も一つあるのかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Yes. There are many different options. Of course, what you're working hard on now might be useful. If you were to continue with the club, one option might be to talk to someone like the principal about the unreasonable aspects.

dialogue.content: ご両親の言葉を聞いて、最後はあなたがどうしたいのか、考えてみる時期なのかも知れないですね。
dialogue.English: Hearing your parents' words, maybe this is a time for you to think about what you ultimately want to do.

dialogue.content: 辞めたいけど、いうと説得される何時間も
dialogue.English: I want to quit, but if I say so, he'll try to persuade me for hours.

dialogue.content: 前に友達が辞めて、
dialogue.English: A friend of mine quit before,

dialogue.content: 大変やった
dialogue.English: and it was a huge ordeal.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。その大変さを思うと、迷いも出てきますね。
dialogue.English: I see. Thinking about that ordeal, it makes you hesitate, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: 親もでてきて保護者会が開かれて校長より強い先生で、、
dialogue.English: Her parents got involved, a parent-teacher meeting was held, and the teacher is more powerful than the principal...

dialogue.content: 私立で強豪校だから、看板なんです
dialogue.English: Because it's a private, powerhouse school, it's their flagship program.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: それは、同じような事が起こると思うと悩んでしまいますね。
dialogue.English: It's understandable that you're worried, thinking the same thing might happen to you.

dialogue.content: 今日は、そろそろお時間になってきましたが。。
dialogue.English: Well, our time is almost up for today...

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Okay, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: あなたの高校生活は、まだまだこれからかと思います。
dialogue.English: You still have a lot of your high school life ahead of you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 卒業される時に、良かったなあと思える時間を過ごして欲しいと思います。
dialogue.English: I hope you can spend your time in a way that you'll look back and think it was good when you graduate.

dialogue.content: 頑張ります
dialogue.English: I'll do my best.

dialogue.content: ええ。応援しています。。本日は、ご相談に来て頂きありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes. I'll be rooting for you. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。それでは、終了メッセージを送らせて頂きます。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'll send the closing message now.
